question: The Corruption Perception Index (CPI) 2024 is released by which global civil society organization?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Transparency International**__.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__
 __ 
• **Transparency International** is a **global civil society organization** established in **1993** to combat corruption worldwide and promote transparency, accountability, and integrity at all levels of government and society. 
• The **Corruption Perceptions Index (CPI)**, released annually by Transparency International, measures the perceived levels of **public sector corruption** in different countries and territories worldwide. 
• The CPI uses a scale from **0 to 100**, where **0** indicates a highly corrupt country and **100** indicates a very clean country. It is widely regarded as a key indicator for understanding global corruption trends. 
• The index is compiled using data from **13 independent surveys and expert assessments** conducted by reputable institutions globally. These sources assess factors like bribery, misuse of public office, and the effectiveness of anti-corruption policies. 
• The **CPI 2024** provides insights into **corruption perception rankings** for nearly **180 countries and territories**, highlighting areas requiring attention for anti-corruption reforms and good governance. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 
• **Transparency International:** 
• Headquartered in **Berlin, Germany**, Transparency International operates globally to fight corruption and promote transparency. 
• It works closely with governments, businesses, and civil society to implement reforms aimed at reducing corruption risks. 
• The organization is known for its advocacy, research, and public campaigns to promote integrity and ethical governance. 
• **Corruption Perceptions Index (CPI):** 
• The CPI is based on a composite of **expert opinions and surveys** from organizations such as the **World Bank**, **World Economic Forum**, and **Economist Intelligence Unit**. 
• Countries with higher scores generally have stronger institutions, better governance, and more robust anti-corruption frameworks. 
• Examples of countries consistently scoring high on the CPI include **Denmark, Finland, and New Zealand**, while countries like **Somalia, Syria, and South Sudan** often rank lower. 
• **Other Organizations Related to Global Governance:** 
• **World Bank:** Focuses on economic development and poverty alleviation globally. It does not specifically release indices like the CPI. 
• **UNODC (United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime):** Primarily tackles issues like drug trafficking, transnational organized crime, and corruption through its programs. 
• **OECD (Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development):** Promotes policies to improve economic and social well-being. It publishes reports on anti-corruption practices but does not release the CPI. 
• **Important Points About Corruption:** 
• Corruption undermines **economic growth, democracy, and social justice**, leading to inefficiencies and inequalities. 
• Effective anti-corruption strategies include strengthening **institutions, enforcing laws, and promoting transparency** in public and private sectors. 
• International conventions such as the **United Nations Convention Against Corruption (UNCAC)** provide a framework for countries to combat corruption collectively. </ul
